subject: chemistry
question_text: Write the chemical equation for the combustion reaction of hexyne.

mark_split.label: The molecular formula and the equation

THE EQUATIONS WERE CHECKED ATOM BY ATOM: C₆H₁₀ + 17/2 O₂ → 6CO₂ + 5H₂O has C 6 = 6, H 10 = 10 and O 17 = 12 + 5 = 17; the doubled form 2C₆H₁₀ + 17O₂ → 12CO₂ + 10H₂O has C 12 = 12, H 20 = 20 and O 34 = 24 + 10 = 34. CONTENT CARRIED BEYOND THE PRINTED ANSWER and to be confirmed by a teacher: the doubled whole-number form, and the statement that hex-1-yne and hex-2-yne give the same combustion equation because the molecular formula is the same.

insider_note: Hexyne is C₆H₁₀ — the -yne ending takes two hydrogen atoms off the alkene, CₙH₂ₙ₋₂. Six carbons and ten hydrogens are what fix 6CO₂ and 5H₂O.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The formula and the equation
lines: The ending -yne means an alkyne, CₙH₂ₙ₋₂.
Hexyne has six carbon atoms, so it is
Six carbons give 6CO₂ and ten hydrogens
A triple bond removes two hydrogen atoms
steps.why: An alkyne carries four hydrogen atoms fewer than the alkane with the same number of carbons, so hexyne is C₆H₁₀ and not C₆H₁₄. Six carbons then give 6CO₂ and ten hydrogens give 5H₂O, which together contain seventeen oxygen atoms.
common_mistakes: Using C₆H₁₂ or C₆H₁₄ for hexyne. Those are the alkene and the alkane; the alkyne is C₆H₁₀.
Writing 5CO₂. Six carbon atoms give six molecules of carbon dioxide.
Expecting the triple bond to change the products. Complete combustion gives CO₂ and water.
steps.memory_tip: The ending -yne means CₙH₂ₙ₋₂: six carbons carry ten hydrogens.
steps.margin_note: Write the molecular formula from the -yne ending before balancing anything.

steps.label: The whole-number form
lines: Atoms: 12 C, 20 H and 34 O on each side.
Hex-1-yne and hex-2-yne are both C₆H₁₀,
so both give this same equation.
steps.why: Doubling clears the half molecule of oxygen, and the atom count confirms the result. Only the molecular formula enters a combustion equation, so the position of the triple bond makes no difference to it.
common_mistakes: Doubling the oxygen alone and leaving the rest. Every coefficient must be doubled together.
Balancing for a named isomer. Combustion depends on the molecular formula only.
steps.memory_tip: Same molecular formula, same combustion equation, whichever hexyne is meant.
steps.margin_note: Give either the fraction form or the doubled form, and check the atom counts.
